notes: First loop; no earlier verdict. As a learning designer I see a sound lesson skeleton: six steps with one stated idea each (src/report/model.ts:24-48), a source legend before any maths (report.txt:85-101), a worked example in the owner's own numbers ('8 x €6.30 = €50.40 ... minus €38.00', report.txt:489), a slider whose explanation updates (report-slider-moved.png), an honest can/cannot box (report.txt:502-514) and a test card with a decision rule agreed before the results (report.txt:847-858). Strong transfer design. What holds it back: (1) the learner never predicts anything before it is revealed; the break-even is handed over in step 1 (report.txt:55) before a single input is introduced. (2) The AI lesson contradicts itself: 'played by an AI' (report.txt:516) sits right above 'with no AI' (report.txt:524). (3) The worst case is taught as a ceiling ('That is the most it can cost', report.txt:405; 'cannot cost more than €560', report.txt:858) although it fixes the 30% switching guess that the report itself says moves the result by €200 (report.txt:425). I did not apply the certainty cap because the sentence starts 'if nobody new comes', but it is close. (4) The feedback loop exists in code (src/report/sections.ts:401) but the demo never shows it.
improvements: Step 4, src/report/sections.ts step4 (around line 311): add one predict-then-check moment before the break-even card. Ask 'How many extra lunch customers a day do you think you need to pay back the test?' with four tappable answers (5 / 7 / 9 / 12), then reveal 9 with feedback specific to the answer (for 7: 'Right for every day after the test, but the €180 setup needs 2 more a day'). Hide or blur the break-even tile in step 1's 'short answer' until then. Why: active learning with feedback; today the only interaction is open exploration. Worked when the UI bot can tap an answer and report.txt shows the tailored feedback above the 9.

Rehearsal AI wording, src/sim/rehearsal.ts:53 (CAVEAT) against src/report/rehearsal.ts:20 (METHOD_WORDS rule-based): make the caveat follow the method. For the demo: 'In this demo the imagined customers follow simple fixed rules. With your AI coach, an AI plays each one from a short description. Either way they are not data.' Why: the theme is learning what AI does and does not do; the demo currently teaches two opposite things two lines apart. Worked when report.txt has exactly one statement about who played the customers and it matches the method.

Worst case and cost cap, src/engine/lunch-offer.ts:301 and src/engine/experiment.ts:136: stop calling €560 'the most it can cost' / 'cannot cost more than'. Say what it rests on and give the range: 'If nobody new comes and 30% of your lunch regulars switch (your guess), the test costs €560; if half of them switch, about €660.' Why: honesty and the misconception 'the worst case is a guarantee'; the report's own 'Which guess matters most' chart shows switching is uncertain. Worked when no owner-facing string claims a ceiling without naming the guess it depends on.

Close the loop in the demo, src/report/sections.ts resultBlock (line 401) and step6: add a 'See an example result' toggle on the demo that renders a clearly labelled sample result (for example 6 extra a day measured, 40% of deal buyers were regulars), with 'Where reality landed' and 'What the test taught you'. Why: feedback and transfer; landing step 7 'Learn' (site/index.html:128) promises it, but a learner cannot see how a guess gets corrected. Worked when the demo report shows a labelled sample result with the Demo data chip and the landing's step 7 links to it.

Decision rule versus sunk cost, src/engine/experiment.ts (decisionRule): 'Keep' starts at 9 a day, yet 'Tweak' says 'From 7 a day the deal already pays its way going forward; the setup is spent either way' (report.txt:853). Teach the sunk-cost idea cleanly: 'Keep if at least 7 a day: the setup is already spent, so only the daily result counts from here. 9 or more means the test also paid for itself.' Why: a money-skills misconception (counting spent money in a go-forward decision) is being modelled by the rule itself. Worked when Keep, Tweak and Stop use the same break-even the step-4 text calls 'pays its way'.

Bridge rehearsal and maths, src/report/rehearsal.ts after 'How far it spread' (line 259): add one sentence that names the tension without merging the two: 'Your likely guess is 8 extra a day. In this rehearsal only 1 of 6 imagined people noticed the board. That does not change the maths; it gives you a question to check: will real people see the board?' Why: prevents both 'the imagined customers prove it will flop' and 'the rehearsal was pointless'. Worked when step 5 states the guess and the rehearsal count side by side with the 'not evidence' reminder.
misconceptionsRisked: The worst case is a guaranteed ceiling ('That is the most it can cost', report.txt:405; 'cannot cost more than €560', report.txt:858), although it holds only at the guessed 30% switching.
An AI played these customers, or no AI did: the demo says both (report.txt:516 and 524), so the learner cannot say what the AI did.

'Expected' is what will happen: the scenario is named 'Expected' (src/engine/lunch-offer.ts:263), and the landing's hero and mini chart show 'expected' ending in profit (site/index.html:52, 108) while the demo's expected loses €56.
Money already spent should decide whether to continue: Keep starts at 9 (includes the spent €180 setup) while 7 is enough going forward (report.txt:850-853).
Nobody in the rehearsal tried it, so the deal will fail: 0 of 6 tried (report.txt:536) with no sentence relating it to the guess of 8 a day.
Precise means certain: −€56.02 to the cent on a round guess of 8 (report.txt:61).
My café already loses money on weekdays: weekday margin €15,287 is shown under fixed costs €16,500 with no explanation (report.txt:238-248).
scaffoldingGaps: No predict-then-check moment anywhere; the slider is exploration without a prior guess.
Concepts used before they are taught: break-even, worst case, 'pays its way' and 'pay back the test' all appear in step 1 (report.txt:54-76).
Two break-evens (9 to pay back the test, 7 to pay its way) under a step called 'The one number to remember' (report.txt:432-441), and neither is in the glossary.
Only one guess can be moved; the least intuitive lesson (regulars switching to a cheaper deal cost €15 a day) is told, never explored hands-on.
The feedback loop (guess vs. what happened) is promised but not demonstrated in the demo.
'What you learned' is told to the learner (report.txt:868-873); there is no retrieval or self-check before it.
